cas.description: The CAs certifly holds keys for, from the root down. Certificates are issued by the CAs at the bottom of the tree.
cas.emptyHint: Start with a root, or with an intermediate whose CSR your existing (offline) root signs.
cas.outsideRootHint: Signed outside certifly; only its certificate is here.
cas.pathLengthHint: How many CA levels may follow below this CA. 0 means none.

new.title: New certificate authority

self_signed.title: Root CA
self_signed.description: A self-signed trust anchor, kept in certifly. Use it only to sign intermediates.

internal.title: Intermediate CA
internal.description: Signed right away by a CA in certifly, for example an L2 under your root or an L3 under an L2.

external.title: Externally signed CA
external.description: certifly creates the key and a CSR; your own root, e.g. an offline one, signs it and you import the certificate.

new.parentHint: The new CA must expire before {date}.
new.noParents: There is no active CA that can sign another CA yet.
new.name: Name
new.slugHint: Part of the public CRL and certificate URLs. Cannot be changed later.
new.subject: Subject
new.validityHint: {years} years. Roots usually last 10 to 20 years, intermediates less.
new.validityExternal: The root that signs the CSR decides the validity.

constraintsHint.self_signed: Optional for a root. Many clients ignore them on a trust anchor.
constraintsHint.internal: Required. They must lie inside the parent's constraints.
constraintsHint.external: Required. Add at least one permitted DNS suffix or IP range.

new.rootWarningTitle: A root key is the most valuable key you have
new.rootWarning: Anyone who can use it can make certificates every client trusts. Use the root only to sign intermediates and issue from those, and keep the master key backup as safe as the root itself.

nc.dnsHint: example.com covers the domain and its subdomains, .example.com only the subdomains.
nc.invalidIp: Not a valid CIDR range, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 or fd00::/8

detail.subject: Subject
detail.noConstraints: This CA has no name constraints.
detail.publicUrlsHint: Anyone can fetch these without signing in. Certificates this CA issues point to them, so they never change.
detail.crlSchedule: A new CRL is published every {validity} hours, {overlap} hours before the current one runs out.
detail.chainHint: The issuers up to the root, as relying parties build the path.
detail.versionsHint: Every certificate this CA has had. Old versions stay so that what they signed can still be checked.
detail.disabledNotice: This CA is disabled. It signs nothing new, but its certificate, chain and CRL stay published.
detail.expiredNotice: This CA's certificate has expired. Renew it to use the CA again.
detail.olderKeyCrls: CRLs of earlier keys, published while certificates they signed are valid
detail.keyCrlUrl: CRL of the current key (embedded in new certificates)
detail.keyCertificateUrl: Certificate of the current key (embedded in new certificates)

csr.title: Sign the certificate request
csr.description: The key stays in certifly. Have the CSR signed by your root, then import the certificate with its chain.
csr.renewDescription: A new key and CSR are waiting. The current certificate keeps working until you import the new one.
csr.step2Hint: For example with OpenSSL. Keep the requested path length and name constraints; certifly refuses the certificate without them.
csr.step3: Import the certificate and the chain up to the root

import.title: Import the CA certificate
import.description: Paste the certificate your root signed and its issuer chain, or choose the files.
import.chainHint: Every intermediate between your root and this CA, and the root itself, as PEM.
import.imported: The certificate was imported and the CA is active

importErrors.invalid_certificate: The certificate could not be read. Paste it as PEM or choose a .pem, .crt or .der file.
importErrors.invalid_chain: The chain could not be read. It must be PEM certificates.
importErrors.public_key_mismatch: The certificate is not for this CA's key. Sign the CSR shown here, not another one.
importErrors.not_ca: The certificate is not a CA certificate (basicConstraints CA:TRUE is missing).
importErrors.path_length_mismatch: The path length differs from the one the CSR requested.
importErrors.missing_key_cert_sign: The key usage must include keyCertSign.
importErrors.missing_crl_sign: The key usage must include cRLSign, or certifly cannot publish CRLs.
importErrors.subject_mismatch: The subject differs from the CSR's.
importErrors.name_constraints_missing: The certificate has no name constraints. Keep the ones the CSR requests.
importErrors.name_constraints_not_critical: The name constraints must be marked critical.
importErrors.chain_incomplete: The chain does not reach a self-signed root. Include every intermediate and the root.
importErrors.chain_signature_invalid: A certificate in the chain is not signed by the next one.
importErrors.chain_issuer_not_ca: A certificate in the chain is not a CA allowed to sign certificates.
importErrors.chain_path_length_exceeded: A CA in the chain does not allow this many levels below it.
importErrors.chain_not_valid_now: A certificate in the chain is not valid right now.
importErrors.not_yet_valid: The certificate is not valid yet.

renew.title: Renew {name}
renew.description: The CA gets a new certificate for the same key, so everything it issued stays valid.
renew.descriptionInternal: {parent} signs a new certificate for the same key. It must expire before {date}.
renew.descriptionExternal: certifly creates a new key and a CSR for it. The current certificate keeps working until you import the one your root signs.
renew.csrCreated: A new CSR is ready to be signed

disable.title: Disable {name}?
disable.description: It will no longer sign certificates, subordinate CAs or renewals. Its certificate, chain and CRL stay published, so what it issued can still be checked. This cannot be undone here.

revoke.title: Revoke {name}?
revoke.description: Its certificates from {parent} go on {parent}'s CRL, and the CA is disabled. Everything it issued stops being trusted. This cannot be undone.
revoke.notice: Revoked on {date} ({reason}) and listed on its parent's CRL. It signs nothing any more.

markCompromised.title: Mark {name} compromised?
markCompromised.description: This CA was signed outside certifly, so certifly cannot revoke it. Marking it compromised disables it and records the reason.
markCompromised.externalSteps: Revoke its certificate at the external root as well, and publish the root's new CRL. Until then relying parties still trust it.
markCompromised.notice: Marked compromised on {date} ({reason}) and disabled. Make sure it is also revoked at the external root that signed it.

hierarchy.title: Hierarchy
hierarchy.hint: Clients that trust {root} accept certificates from this CA.
hierarchy.hintRoot: Clients must trust this root directly, for example through a trust bundle.

templates.description: A template holds the rules a certificate is issued under: which CA signs it, which names it may carry, its usages and lifetime.
templates.emptyHint: Create a template from a preset to start issuing certificates.
templates.rootWarning: Every certificate from this template is signed with the root key, which then has to stay online. Prefer an issuing CA below the root.
templates.ttlExceedsCa: The CA runs out in {days} days, sooner than the maximum lifetime. Certificates are cut back to the CA's end.

webserver_tls.title: Webserver TLS
webserver_tls.description: HTTPS for websites and APIs. DNS names required.

mtls_server.title: mTLS server
mtls_server.description: The server side of mutual TLS. DNS names required.

mtls_client.title: mTLS client
mtls_client.description: Clients that prove who they are: devices, services, people. Needs a common name; DNS, email and URI (SPIFFE) names optional.

server_client.title: Server and client
server_client.description: One certificate for both sides, e.g. nodes in a cluster. DNS names required.

form.name: Name
form.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Cannot be changed later.
form.caConstraintsHint: The name rules below must stay inside them.
form.noCas: There is no active CA to bind a template to. Create a CA first.
form.rsaOnlyHint: Key and data encipherment are only set for RSA keys.
form.namesHint: Only names matching these rules are allowed; an empty list allows none.
form.allowedDnsHint: *.example.com matches one label below, **.example.com any depth.

form.defaultTagsHint: Added to every certificate issued with this template. Can be changed when issuing.

detail.archivedNotice: This template is archived. Nothing more is issued or renewed with it; certificates it issued stay valid.

archive.title: Archive {name}?
archive.description: Nothing more can be issued or renewed with this template. Certificates it issued stay valid. This cannot be undone.

acme.name: ACME
acme.hint: Clients such as certbot, cert-manager or Caddy request certificates from this template. Each new ACME account needs an EAB key from the list below. Challenges: http-01 and tls-alpn-01. Wildcard names cannot be ordered over ACME.
acme.enabled: ACME is on for this template
acme.disabled: ACME is off for this template
acme.none: No EAB keys yet. Clients need one to create an ACME account.
acme.revokeText: New accounts can no longer use it, and accounts bound to it can no longer order certificates. Issued certificates stay valid.

est.name: EST
est.hint: Devices enroll over EST with a username and password from the list below, and re-enroll with their current certificate, which your TLS proxy passes on.
est.enabled: EST is on for this template
est.disabled: EST is off for this template
est.none: No credentials yet. Devices need one to enroll.
est.revokeText: Devices can no longer enroll with it. Issued certificates stay valid, and re-enrolling with them keeps working.

certificates.description: Certificates certifly issued, and those imported from elsewhere to track their expiry.
certificates.emptyHint: Issue one from a template, by pasting a CSR or letting certifly generate the key.

key.csrHint: PEM or DER. The signature is checked.
key.reuseHint: The new certificate uses the same key as before, from the CSR stored with this certificate.
key.keygenHint: The private key is shown once and never stored.

issue.title: Issue certificate
issue.noTemplates: There is no active template you can issue with. An admin creates templates.
issue.commonNameCsrHint: Leave empty to use the CSR's common name.
issue.sansCsrHint: Leave the list empty to use the names in the CSR.
issue.ttlHint: At most {max} days for this template.

issue.ignoredFields: The template does not let requests set these subject fields, so they were left out: {fields}

privateKey.title: Private key, shown only once
privateKey.oncePem: Download or copy it now. certifly does not keep it: once you leave this page it is gone, and a lost key means issuing a new certificate.
privateKey.oncePkcs12: Download the PKCS#12 file now; it holds the key and the chain, protected by your password. certifly does not keep it: once you leave this page it is gone.
privateKey.leaveConfirm: The private key is shown only once and will be gone. Leave this page?

downloads.title: Downloads
downloads.hint: The certificate, its chain up to the root, and the full bundle servers expect.
downloads.hintNoKey: The certificate, its chain up to the root, and the full bundle servers expect. certifly has no private key to offer.
downloads.hintImported: The certificate as it was imported. certifly has neither its chain nor its private key.

detail.expiredNotice: This certificate has expired. Renew it to get a new one with the same names.
detail.renewDueNotice: This certificate is close to expiry. Renew it soon.
detail.verifyHint: After downloading the certificate and the chain, this checks the certificate against the chain and prints its fields.
detail.importedNotice: Imported from elsewhere. certifly tracks its expiry but cannot revoke or renew it; do that with its issuer.

renew.title: Renew certificate
renew.description: Issues a new certificate with the same template, subject and names. This one is marked as superseded.

revoke.title: Revoke {name}?
revoke.description: Revoked certificates go on the CRL of the CA key that signed them within moments. This cannot be undone.
revoke.notice: Revoked on {date} ({reason}). It is listed on its CA's CRL until it expires.

import.title: Import certificates
import.description: Add certificates issued elsewhere to the inventory, so they show here, on the dashboard and in expiry alerts. certifly cannot revoke or renew them.

hints.affiliation_changed: The name or owner in the certificate changed.
hints.superseded: A newer certificate replaces this one.

trustBundles.description: Named sets of CA certificates, published as one PEM file at a public URL, for client trust stores and mTLS settings such as nginx's ssl_client_certificate.
trustBundles.emptyHint: Group the CAs that clients should trust, and point them at one URL.
trustBundles.withChain: Includes the chain to the root
trustBundles.deleteDescription: Its public URL stops working; clients that fetch it will get an error.
trustBundles.publicUrlHint: Anyone can fetch this without signing in. It changes as the CAs in it are renewed.
trustBundles.contentsHint: What the PEM holds right now: the current certificate of each chosen CA (and of earlier keys still in use).
trustBundles.contentsHintChain: What the PEM holds right now: each chosen CA's certificates and their issuers up to the root.
trustBundles.noCertificates: No valid certificates: the chosen CAs are expired or revoked.

form.name: Name
form.slugHint: Part of the public URL. Cannot be changed later.
form.casHint: The PEM lists them in the order you pick them.
form.noCas: There are no CAs with a certificate yet.
form.includeChain: Include the chain to the root
form.includeChainHint: Adds each CA's issuers so clients can verify the full chain.
form.traefikHint: Lets Traefik load this bundle through its HTTP provider, with the certificates inline.
form.traefikClientAuthHint: Adds a TLS option that makes Traefik check client certificates against this bundle.
form.traefikTransportHint: Adds a servers transport that trusts backends whose certificates were issued by this bundle's CAs.
form.traefikRequireTokenHint: Traefik sends this bundle's token in an Authorization header. It is generated when you save and shown once.

traefik.title: Traefik
traefik.info: Add the static configuration to Traefik. It polls the endpoint and picks up renewed CAs by itself.
traefik.regenerateDescription: The current token stops working at once. Update Traefik with the new one.
traefik.tokenWarning: Copy it now. It is shown only once.

alerts.description: Get an email or a webhook call when certificates or CAs are about to expire, are issued or revoked, or a CRL cannot be published.

eventHints.expiring: Checked once a day. Each threshold is sent once per certificate.
eventHints.ca_expiring: Checked once a day. Each threshold is sent once per CA certificate.
eventHints.revoked: Every revoked certificate, and CAs revoked or marked compromised.
eventHints.crl_failed: A CRL could not be built or signed; sent at most once a day per CA.
eventHints.ssh_host_expiring: Checked once a day. Each threshold is sent once per SSH host certificate. A certificate that was already renewed is not reported.

alerts.deleteChannelDescription: It is removed from every rule. Its delivery history stays.
alerts.deleteRuleDescription: No more alerts are sent for it. Its delivery history stays.

rules.description: What to alert about, and where to send it.
rules.channelFirst: Add a channel first: rules send to channels.
rules.dialogDescription: Leave CAs and templates empty to cover all of them.
rules.name: Name
rules.includeImportedHint: Certificates from the inventory, which have no CA or template here.

channels.description: Email recipients and webhooks that rules send to.
channels.secretHint: Copy it now: it is shown only once. Use it to check the X-Certifly-Signature header of each call.
channels.signatureHint: Each call is a JSON POST. X-Certifly-Signature is sha256= and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with this secret. Reject calls whose X-Certifly-Timestamp is more than a few minutes old.
channels.dialogDescription: Where alerts go: a list of email addresses or a webhook.
channels.name: Name
channels.recipientsHint: One address per line, up to 20.
channels.urlHint: http or https. Redirects are not followed; the receiver has 10 seconds to answer.
channels.rotateHint: A new secret replaces the current one at once.

deliveries.description: Every alert sent or attempted. Failed webhooks and mails are retried a few times with growing delays.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Group and filter certificates. Templates can add tags to the certificates they issue.
tags.name: Name
tags.deleteText: It is removed from {count} certificates and from every template. This cannot be undone.

access.emptyHint: An admin adds you to a group that has access to a host group.
access.getCliTip: The CLI signs your key, keeps the certificate renewed in ssh-agent and lists the hosts you can reach. It signs in through your browser.

sign.title: Sign my key
sign.cliTip: The certifly CLI signs your key and renews it for you. Install it from My SSH access.
sign.noHostGroups: No host group to sign for.
sign.attestedOnly: This host group needs an attested YubiKey key. Use the certifly CLI to sign it.
sign.publicKeyTip: Paste your public key, the contents of a .pub file such as ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub.
sign.publicKeyTipSk: This host group needs a YubiKey key. Paste the .pub file of an ed25519-sk or ecdsa-sk key.
sign.lifetimeTip: The host group's default is {default}. The longest it allows is {max}.

detail.deleteText: Its access rules and join tokens are deleted. A host group with hosts cannot be deleted.

form.name: Name
form.slugTip: Part of every principal, such as prod:root. It cannot be changed later.
form.hostNamesTip: The names of the hosts in this group. A host can only join with names that match. * stands for one part of a name, ** for several.
form.invalidPattern: Use a host name like web.prod.corp, *.prod.corp or **.prod.corp.
form.ttlTip: How long a user certificate lasts. People can ask for less than the longest lifetime.
form.defaultAboveMax: The default cannot be longer than the longest lifetime.
form.keyPolicyTip: Any accepts every key. YubiKey needs a hardware key of type ed25519-sk or ecdsa-sk. Attested also checks the YubiKey's attestation, which only the CLI sends.
form.forceCommandTip: Every login with a certificate from this group runs this command and nothing else.
form.sourceAddressTip: Certificates only work when the login comes from one of these addresses or ranges. Leave empty for any address.
form.invalidAddress: Use an IP address or a range like 10.0.0.0/8.
form.hostTtlTip: How long a host certificate lasts. The host renews it well before it ends.

sshRules.deleteText: People in the group get no login here with their next certificate. Certificates they hold stay valid until they end.

dialog.noGroups: Every group already has a rule here.
dialog.loginsPlaceholder: Type a login and press Enter
dialog.invalidLogin: Use a login name like deploy or root.
dialog.ownUsernameTip: Each person can also log in as their own SSH username on these hosts.

sshJoinTokens.label: Label
sshJoinTokens.validTip: The token can enrol one host within this time, at most 7 days.
sshJoinTokens.deleteText: It can no longer enrol a host. Hosts that joined with it keep working.

sshHosts.emptyHint: Hosts join with a join token from their host group, or an operator adds them here.
sshHosts.emptyInGroup: No hosts in this host group yet.

dialog.hostNamesTipNone: The host group has no name patterns yet.
dialog.invalidName: Use a host name like web-01.prod.corp.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameTip: Shown in lists. Defaults to the first host name.
dialog.keysTip: One per line, from /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub. Changing names or keys revokes the host's certificates.

detail.noCertificate: No certificate yet. The host gets one when it first syncs.

revoke.title: Revoke this certificate?
revoke.description: {keyId} goes on the revocation list of its SSH CA. Hosts pick it up with their next sync.

new.title: New SSH CA
new.name: Name
new.slugTip: Used in the public URLs of the CA key and revocation list. It cannot be changed later.
new.keyTip: certifly keeps the private key encrypted and never shows it again. One key signs user and host certificates.
new.privateKeyTip: An unencrypted OpenSSH or PKCS#8 private key. Ed25519, ECDSA P-256 and P-384 and RSA of 2048 bits and more work.

detail.deleteText: The key is destroyed. A CA with host groups or certificates cannot be deleted.
detail.manualTip: For hosts without the CLI. Save the public key and the revocation list on the host, add the sshd_config lines and reload sshd. Add the known_hosts line on the machines that connect.

detail.deleteText: Its access rules are deleted with it. People lose the logins it gave them with their next certificate.
detail.removeText: They lose the logins this group gives with their next certificate.
detail.providerGroupsTip: People whose identity provider lists one of these group names join this group when they sign in, and leave it when it is no longer listed.
detail.notUsed: No host group uses this group yet.
